So after finishing "The God Delusion" by Dawkins, I'm craving more rational scientific thought on the matter. What are your suggestions?

Godel, Escher, Bach. By Hofstadler.

He explores the relationships of Maths, music and arts in the conscious mind and the nature of the epiphenominon that is self-awareness.
Read the Summa Theologica, if you want to truly be rational, then its fantastic to challenge your thoughts, as I do despite being an atheist
read A Universe From Nothing by Lawrence Krauss. he's a cosmologist and theoretical physicist, a great mind and an interesting author.

The Believing Brain: From Ghosts and Gods to Politics and Conspiracies---How We Construct Beliefs and Reinforce Them as Truths

By none other that Michael Shermer.
If you haven't read it yet, check out The Age of Reason, by Thomas Paine.

If you want to continue with more Dawkins, I actually think The Greatest Show On Earth is better than The God Delusion. TGD is Why Creationists Are Wrong while TGSOE is Why Scientists Are Right, a subtle distinction but I greatly prefer it.
